extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and patent office staff preparing or processing Hague (international) design applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, filing, and obtaining an international (Hague) registration for industrial designs, including filing-date rules, required contents, language, fees, and US-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date — international application filed directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application is filed directly with the International Bureau, the filing date shall, subject to paragraph (3), be the date on which the International Bureau receives the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Article 9(1). Filing date is the date IB receives the application unless an irregularity entailing a postponement exists. (Related discussion: MPEP § 2906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date — international application filed indirectly (through an Office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application is filed through the Office of the applicant's Contracting Party, the filing date shall be determined as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Article 9(2) and Rule 13: if governed exclusively by the 1999 Act, the filing date is the date the Office received the application provided the IB receives it within one month (or six months if security clearance is required); otherwise the filing date is the date the IB receives the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities entailing postponement of the filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application has, on the date on which it is received by the International Bureau, an irregularity prescribed as entailing a postponement of the filing date, the filing date shall be the date on which the correction of such irregularity is received by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The irregularities prescribed as entailing postponement include: (a) application not in a prescribed language; (b) any of the following elements missing: (i) an express or implicit indication that international registration under the 1999 Act or the 1960 Act is sought; (ii) indications allowing identity of applicant to be established; (iii) indications sufficient to enable applicant or representative to be contacted; (iv) a reproduction or specimen of each industrial design; (v) designation of at least one Contracting Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits to correct irregularities (invitation period)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the International Bureau finds that the application does not fulfill applicable requirements, it shall invite the applicant to make the required corrections within three months from the date of the invitation; if fees received are less than the basic fee for one design, the IB may invite payment of at least the basic fee within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Rule 14(1)(a) and (b). Failure to timely correct may result in abandonment or loss of designation for certain defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment and reimbursement for failure to remedy irregularities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an irregularity (other than an irregularity referred to in Article 8(2)(b) of the 1999 Act) is not remedied within the time limit, the international application shall be considered abandoned and the International Bureau shall refund any fees paid after deduction of an amount corresponding to the basic fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Rule 14(3). For defects under Article 8(2)(b), failure to timely comply may result in the application being deemed not to contain the designation of the Contracting Party concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed languages
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be in English, French or Spanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Rule 6(1). Non-prescribed language is an irregularity entailing postponement of filing date (Rule 14(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: International registration — timing of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall register each industrial design immediately upon receipt of the international application or, where corrections are invited under Article 8, immediately upon receipt of the required corrections; registration is effected whether or not publication is deferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Article 10(1) and Rule 15(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of the international registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, the date of the international registration shall be the filing date of the international application; where an irregularity relates to Article 5(2), the date of registration shall be the date the correction is received or the filing date, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Article 10(2). MPEP explains that Article 5(2) requirements can shift the registration date to the date of timely correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The international registration shall contain: (i) all the data contained in the international application (except certain priority claims), (ii) any reproduction of the industrial design, (iii) the date of the international registration, (iv) the number of the international registration, (v) the relevant class of the International Classification as determined by the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Rule 15(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of the international application (Article 5(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be in a prescribed language and shall contain or be accompanied by: (i) a request for international registration; (ii) prescribed data concerning the applicant; (iii) prescribed copies of a reproduction or specimens of each industrial design presented in the prescribed manner; (iv) an indication of the product(s) which constitute the industrial design or in relation to which the industrial design is to be used; (v) an indication of the designated Contracting Parties; (vi) the prescribed fees; (vii) any other prescribed particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Article 5(1) and Rule 7. Additional specific details and presentation requirements are set forth in Rule 7 and Rules 9–12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional mandatory contents required by certain Contracting Parties (Article 5(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting Party whose Office is an Examining Office and whose law requires certain elements for a filing date may notify the Director General; the elements include: (i) indications concerning the identity of the creator; (ii) a brief description of the reproduction or of the characteristic features; (iii) a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the international application contains the designation of a Contracting Party that has made such a notification, the application shall also contain, in the prescribed manner, the element(s) that were the subject of that notification. See Article 5(2) and Rule 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be presented on the official form and shall be signed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 7(1). Applications not on the official form or unsigned may be defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — payment, amount and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed fees applicable to the international application shall be paid as provided for in Rules 27 and 28; the application must indicate the amount of fees being paid and the method of payment or instructions to debit an account with the IB, and identify the party effecting the payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 7(2) and Rule 7(3)(vii). If fees received are less than the basic fee, IB may invite payment within two months (Rule 14(1)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identity and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall contain the name of the applicant given in accordance with the Administrative Instructions, the address and email address of the applicant, and indications allowing the identity of the applicant to be established and enabling the applicant or its representative to be contacted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 7(3)(i)–(iii) and Article 5(1)(ii). These items are mandatory; missing contact/identity information is an irregularity that can postpone filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product identification and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication of the product or products which constitute the industrial design or in relation to which the industrial design is to be used, as prescribed; the product(s) shall preferably be identified by using terms appearing in the list of goods of the International Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Article 5(1)(iv) and Rule 7(3)(iv). All products in the application must belong to the same class of the International Classification (Rule 7(7)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on number of designs and reproductions
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of industrial designs included in the international application may not exceed 100, and the number of reproductions or specimens accompanying the international application must conform to Rules 9 or 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 7(3)(v) and MPEP § 2909. Applications exceeding limits or improper reproduction counts risk noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Contracting Parties and applicant's Contracting Party indication
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall indicate the designated Contracting Parties and, where applicable, the Contracting Party or Parties in respect of which the applicant fulfills the conditions to be the holder of an international registration; for designations under the 1999 Act, the application shall contain the indication of the applicant’s Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Article 5(1)(v), Rule 7(3)(iii) and Rule 7(4)(a). Failure to include required designation information can affect effects in particular Contracting Parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional contents and permitted additions
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application may optionally contain: two or more industrial designs (subject to conditions), a request for deferment or immediate publication, optional inclusion of elements of Article 5(2)(b), representative name and address, priority claims under Paris Convention, declarations concerning exhibitions, requests for deferred publication, and statements identifying information known to applicant material to eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Article 5(4)–(5) and Rule 7(5). Optional inclusion of elements may be strategic (e.g., include description or creator even if not required by designated CP).

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional matter permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application contains any matter other than that required or permitted by the 1999 Act, the 1960 Act, the Regulations or the Administrative Instructions, the International Bureau shall delete it ex officio; accompanying documents not required or permitted may be disposed of by the IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 7(6). Avoid attaching extraneous documents or content that are not explicitly allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: All products to be in the same International Classification class
rubrics_metrics.description: All the products which constitute the industrial designs to which an international application relates, or in relation to which the industrial designs are to be used, shall belong to the same class of the International Classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 7(7). Mixing products across classes is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hague Administrative Instructions — permitted matters and required formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted matters include: (a) a DAS code accompanying a priority claim; (b) indication/claim and certificate of economic status for reduced fees; (c) a Declaration Concerning Exception to Lack of Novelty in prescribed wording and indication of designs concerned (with optional accompanying documentation); (d) statements in formats established by the IB for certain Rule 7(5)(g) statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hague Administrative Instructions Section 408. Follow prescribed wording and formats for declarations and supporting documentation when invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: US-specific required contents when the United States is designated
rubrics_metrics.description: An international design application that designates the United States shall contain or be accompanied by: (1) a claim; (2) indications concerning the identity of the creator (inventor) in accordance with Rule 11(1); and (3) the inventor's oath or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.1021(d). Presentation of inventor identification and related information in the international application prior to international registration will be considered to satisfy certain oath/declaration requirements (see §§ 1.63 and 1.64 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: US filing date — effective registration date (35 U.S.C. 384)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to subsection (b), the filing date of an international design application in the United States shall be the effective registration date (the date of international registration determined by the International Bureau).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 35 U.S.C. 384(b), an applicant may request review by the Director of the filing date in the United States; the Director may establish procedures (including a surcharge) to review and may determine a different US filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to accord a different US filing date (37 CFR 1.1023)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant believes the international design application is entitled under the Hague Agreement to a filing date in the United States other than the date of international registration, the applicant may petition the Director to accord the application a filing date in the United States other than the date of international registration; such petition must be accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(f) and include a showing to the satisfaction of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.1023(b). This is the procedural avenue to request a US filing date different from the IB's effective registration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of contents into categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of an international design application fall into three categories: (1) mandatory contents; (2) additional mandatory contents; and (3) optional contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2909 summary. Identify which items are unconditional requirements, which depend on designation/Contracting Party notifications, and which are elective when assembling the application.
